basic_info: Patient name: Wayne. Age: late 40s (exact age unknown). Gender: male. Chief complaint: left shoulder pain for about three weeks, constant, worsens with lifting or lying on the shoulder at night.
present_illness: Left shoulder pain for approximately three weeks. Pain is constant and worsens with lifting or lying on the affected shoulder at night. The pain is described as a constant ache that becomes sharper with arm movement or pressure. No numbness or weakness is reported. The patient has experienced stiffness in the left shoulder, making it difficult to reach behind the back or lift objects, and has avoided putting pressure on the shoulder, especially at night.

No history of serious shoulder issues. No history of repetitive overhead activities or heavy lifting. No history of diabetes, thyroid disorders, or autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis or lupus. Recent basement work may have contributed to overuse or strain.
